## Overview

A name whispered in dread  -  the century of suffering that nearly saw the extinction of all mortal races. The Abominable End marks the 200-year period during which an endless tide of monsters poured through planar breaches along the coast of Kythoria, pushing mortal civilization to the brink of annihilation.

## Date

Approximately **400 years ago** to **200 years ago**  -  a two-century-long cataclysm.

## Causes

The monster invasion was not a natural catastrophe. It was a **deliberate act of divine genocide** orchestrated by the gods (fragments of the Originals A and C), who had wanted to destroy mortalkind since before the Great Sacrifice. Unable to destroy mortals directly, they struck pacts with the Abyss, Nine Hells, Shadowfell, and Feywild to supply an endless tide of monsters.

The gods opened **planar breaches** along the entire coast of Kythoria, through which the monster hordes poured forth.

## The Invasion

For two centuries, the mortal races were steadily pushed back. Kingdoms fell. Cities were overrun. The mortal races were driven from their ancestral homelands, fleeing inward as the monster tide consumed everything behind them.

The monster army eventually consolidated under **Five Major Generals**, the most powerful creatures to emerge from its ranks. These generals commanded the largest armies and coordinated the assault that pushed the mortal races to their final retreat.

## Outcome

The mortal races were pushed to the brink of extinction, clinging to the center-southeast of the continent. Here, they made their final stand and founded three capital cities  -  Skywatch, Emberforge, and Weaveheart  -  collectively known as **the Last Stand**.

## Aftermath

The Last Stand's formation marked the end of The Abominable End and the beginning of **The Rise of the Mortals**. A magical barrier was developed, creating a safe haven. From this bastion, the mortal races organized the **First Alliance** and began the slow, determined reconquering of Kythoria.

The Abominable End is remembered as a time of unimaginable cruelty and suffering  -  a scar on the collective memory of every mortal race. Its horrors shape the culture, politics, and psychology of the present day.
